This is a **finding** in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

### Cause
When a patient replies to the self-pay prompt with `"I'll self-pay"` or `"I'll pay for it myself"` (generated by [`Voice._selfpay`](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L115-L124)), [`explicit_selfpay`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L170-L178) returns `None`:
- `"I'll self-pay"` matches `\b(self-pay|self pay|out of pocket|pay myself)\b`, but fails the second required conjunct `\b(i choose|i'll pay|i will pay|i'll do|i want|choose|paying|go with|yes)\b`.
- `"I'll pay for it myself"` matches `\bi'll pay\b`, but fails the first conjunct because `"for it"` separates `"pay"` and `"myself"`.

In [`Driver.book`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L422-L431), when `explicit_selfpay(u)` is `None` after `asked_selfpay` is set, it calls [`Driver.consent`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271). Under Arm F (`consent_in_code=True`), `Driver.consent` treats a model `"yes"` as `None`, so `Driver.book` calls `self.unclear("selfpay", ...)` and re-asks the patient instead of advancing the booking.

The failure is in the frozen driver's self-pay parser and booking consent flow ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L170-L178), [Driver.book](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L422-L431)), which fails to recognize valid self-pay phrasings produced by [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L115-L124).

Specifically:
- `"I'll self-pay"` matches the first regex in `explicit_selfpay` (`\b(self-pay|self pay|out of pocket|pay myself)\b`), but fails the second regex (`\b(i choose|i'll pay|i will pay|i'll do|i want|choose|paying|go with|yes)\b`).
- `"I'll pay for it myself"` (and `"That's fine, I'll just pay for it myself"`) fails the first regex because `"pay"` and `"myself"` are separated by `"for it"`.
- When `explicit_selfpay` returns `None` after `asked_selfpay` is set, `Driver.book` calls `self.consent("selfpay", ...)`, which under Arm F (`consent_in_code=True`) treats a model `"yes"` as `None` and re-asks via `self.unclear`.

In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L170-L178), `explicit_selfpay` requires **both** a self-pay noun/phrase (`self-pay`, `self pay`, `out of pocket`, `pay myself`) **and** a separate action phrase (`i choose`, `i'll pay`, `i will pay`, `i'll do`, `i want`, `choose`, `paying`, `go with`, `yes`).

- `"I'll self-pay"` ([voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L118-L119)) matches the first regex (`self-pay`) but fails the second (`i'll self-pay` does not match `i'll pay` or `i'll do`).
- `"I'll pay for it myself"` and `"That's fine, I'll just pay for it myself"` ([voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L120-L124)) fail the first regex because `"for it"` sits between `"pay"` and `"myself"`.

As a result, `explicit_selfpay` returns `None`. In [`Driver.book`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L422-L443), when `asked_selfpay` is already set and `consent_in_code=True` (Arm F), `Driver.consent` treats the reader model's `"yes"` as `None`, so `Driver.book` falls through to `self.unclear("selfpay", ...)` and asks the patient again (then hands off on the second unclear). Because `dcitl_port.py` is the frozen reference driver, this is a `finding`.
